context.alert_text: Errors on the search API function above 20 per minute

root_cause.hypothesis: An AppConfig deployment (deployment=9, version=12) to warden-dev-search/dev was rolled back, but the rollback has not completed, so the search-api lambda is still exercising the bad config values that trigger an IndexError in ranking_v3.py (around the score_key lookup), causing a spike in Errors without any change in invocation volume, duration, memory, or throttling.
evidence: C1: appconfig rollback state=ROLLED_BACK but completed=not yet on version 12
F5/F6/F7: repeated IndexError at ranking_v3.py lines 71-77 tied to key=score_key
M4/M6/M7: throttles=0, duration well under timeout, low concurrency rule out resource exhaustion
C3: no infra/code deploy in the 6h window, pointing away from a code deploy and toward the config change
ruled_out: Lambda resource starvation (memory/timeout) - M6 duration max 140ms vs 6s timeout, M2 memory 1024MB, no OOM signals
A code deploy - C3 explicitly shows no change on the lambda in the window

proposal.reasoning: The AppConfig deployment to warden-dev-search/dev shows a rollback that has not completed, and the application is throwing IndexError exceptions consistent with bad config-driven indexing (score_key) rather than a resource or infra problem. Forcing/completing the revert to the prior stable AppConfig version should remove the bad values causing the IndexError spike.
proposal.expected_effect: search-api lambda resumes using the last known-good AppConfig version, eliminating the IndexError traceback pattern and bringing lambda_errors back under the alarm threshold.

reasons: none of the cited evidence bears on revert_config (it names none of: appconfig, feature flag, feature-flag, configuration profile, toggle...).
target 'appconfig:warden-dev-search/dev' is a pattern or a list, not one resource.
